stem: Which Azure service brings together metrics, logs, traces, and events to help understand application and infrastructure behavior?

choices.D: Azure Resource Manager templates

explanations.A: Policy evaluates and enforces governance rules rather than acting as the primary telemetry platform.
explanations.B: Cost Management addresses expenditure and usage analysis rather than all operational telemetry.
explanations.C: Monitor is the Azure telemetry collection and analysis service.
explanations.D: Templates declare deployment infrastructure rather than collect runtime observations.

stem: A team wants a time series of a resource's numerical CPU utilization measurements. Which telemetry form best matches?

choices.D: Service Health maintenance notices

explanations.A: Metrics represent numerical measurements over time.
explanations.B: Tags are management metadata rather than a CPU time series.
explanations.C: Templates describe desired infrastructure rather than measured CPU behavior.
explanations.D: Maintenance communications do not supply the resource's CPU measurements.

stem: An investigator needs the context and fields of individual recorded events rather than only a numeric trend. Which data form is most useful?

choices.D: Logs

explanations.A: An average can summarize a trend but omit individual event context.
explanations.B: A budget is a financial threshold rather than an event record.
explanations.C: Location metadata does not contain individual runtime events.
explanations.D: Log records can carry detailed event context that supports filtering and analysis.

stem: Which Azure portal experience is primarily used to edit and run KQL queries against Azure Monitor Logs?

choices.D: Resource-group lock management

explanations.A: The calculator estimates spending rather than querying monitoring logs.
explanations.B: Log Analytics provides the interactive log-query experience.
explanations.C: Advisor suggestions do not replace the KQL log-query editor.
explanations.D: Lock management protects resources from certain control-plane changes rather than analyzing logs.

stem: What role does a Log Analytics workspace have in a monitoring design?

choices.A: It automatically grants Owner access to every resource in a tenant
choices.B: It provides a storage and access boundary for collected log data
choices.C: It replaces every source application's instrumentation
choices.D: It guarantees that every possible Azure data operation is already recorded

explanations.A: A workspace does not confer tenant-wide resource ownership.
explanations.B: Workspaces support the organization and analysis of monitoring log data.
explanations.C: Data still needs an appropriate collection path.
explanations.D: Collection and data availability depend on configuration and source capabilities.

stem: A team wants to inspect Azure resource creation and configuration-change events. Which log is the appropriate starting point?

choices.D: Only a pricing estimate

explanations.A: The Activity log records control-plane resource-management events.
explanations.B: Request traces concern application behavior rather than all Azure management operations.
explanations.C: Stored payloads are not the subscription's management-event history.
explanations.D: An estimate does not record which management operations occurred.

stem: Users report a slow web request, and the developer wants request and dependency-call context. Which Monitor feature is designed for application performance investigation?

choices.D: Application Insights

explanations.A: Locks control management changes rather than observe request performance.
explanations.B: Compliance findings do not replace request and dependency telemetry.
explanations.C: Budgets concern spending rather than transaction timing.
explanations.D: Application Insights helps analyze suitably collected application requests and dependencies.

stem: Which statement correctly describes Application Insights in relation to Azure Monitor?

choices.A: It is the service that assigns management-group membership
choices.B: It is only an offline server-migration appliance
choices.C: It is Azure Monitor's application performance monitoring feature
choices.D: It replaces Azure's resource deployment control plane

explanations.A: Management groups are part of Azure governance and hierarchy, not Application Insights.
explanations.B: That describes a different capability from application monitoring.
explanations.C: Application Insights extends the monitoring experience with application telemetry analysis.
explanations.D: Application monitoring is not the resource deployment control plane.

stem: An application runs in Azure but emits no relevant application telemetry. What must a developer consider before expecting useful request traces?

choices.D: Only dismissing an Advisor recommendation

explanations.A: Tags do not instrument request execution.
explanations.B: Control-plane logs do not supply all custom request traces.
explanations.C: Application Insights requires a suitable data-collection path for the desired application observations.
explanations.D: Recommendation state does not establish application instrumentation.

stem: Which part of an Azure Monitor alert rule determines when the selected signal should trigger an alert?

choices.C: Only an application's source repository URL
choices.D: The condition

explanations.A: A receiver address determines a delivery destination rather than the signal threshold.
explanations.B: A display name does not define an operational threshold.
explanations.C: A repository link does not define the monitored signal's condition.
explanations.D: The condition evaluates whether the monitored signal meets the specified criteria.

stem: What does an action group primarily configure for an alert design?

choices.C: The source application's full business logic
choices.D: The target resource's Azure region pairing

explanations.A: Action groups define reusable receivers or actions used by alert rules.
explanations.B: Values come from the monitoring data source rather than receiver configuration.
explanations.C: An action group does not define the whole application.
explanations.D: Receiver configuration does not determine Azure geography.

stem: An alert condition fires, but an intended operator receives no message. Which area should be checked?

choices.A: Only whether the source resource has a friendly name
choices.B: The associated action group and notification delivery configuration
choices.C: Only whether Azure Advisor has cost suggestions
choices.D: Only whether a deployment template compiles

explanations.A: A friendly name does not verify a working notification route.
explanations.B: Triggering and notification delivery are distinct parts of the alert workflow.
explanations.C: Cost advice does not establish receiver delivery.
explanations.D: Template compilation alone does not prove the alert's notification routing.

stem: Which monitoring choice is most suitable for detecting a numerical latency threshold over a defined interval?

choices.A: A metric alert on the appropriate latency signal and aggregation
choices.D: A storage account's redundancy setting alone

explanations.A: Metric conditions can evaluate numerical measurements over specified windows.
explanations.B: A deletion lock does not evaluate latency measurements.
explanations.C: A location restriction does not detect runtime latency.
explanations.D: Redundancy does not itself configure a latency alert.

stem: A team wants to alert when a KQL query finds a defined set of failure records. Which alert type fits?

choices.D: A log search alert

explanations.A: A lock prevents certain changes rather than evaluates query results.
explanations.B: Budget thresholds concern cost rather than the specified failure query.
explanations.C: A bookmark does not execute and evaluate the KQL failure query.
explanations.D: Log search alerts evaluate query results from collected monitoring logs.

stem: Why can a whole-day mean response time miss a short but severe slowdown?

choices.A: Azure Monitor never supports numerical measurements
choices.B: An average always equals the slowest request
choices.C: Aggregation over a long window can hide short periods and outliers
choices.D: A resource-group tag automatically removes slow samples

explanations.A: Monitor supports metrics and other telemetry.
explanations.B: An average is different from a maximum or a high percentile.
explanations.C: Window and aggregation choices affect which operational problems are visible.
explanations.D: Tags do not inherently filter application timing records.

stem: What does the KQL where operator do in the lab's synthetic example?

choices.A: Writes the selected records into the source application's database
choices.B: Filters records that meet the specified expression
choices.D: Changes the workspace's Azure region

explanations.A: This query operator does not perform that application write.
explanations.B: The example retains records whose Success value is false.
explanations.C: Filtering records does not create a notification destination.
explanations.D: A log query filter does not relocate a workspace.

stem: What does summarize count() by Name accomplish in a log query?

choices.A: Counts records separately for each Name value
choices.C: Deletes all records that share a name
choices.D: Adds the Name field to every resource's ownership tags

explanations.A: Grouping makes an aggregate for each name represented by the selected records.
explanations.B: A query aggregation is not an infrastructure deployment.
explanations.C: Summarization does not perform that deletion.
explanations.D: Log aggregation does not mutate Azure resource tags.

stem: In the synthetic data, failed requests have durations 900 ms and 1100 ms. What mean does filtering failures and averaging duration produce?

explanations.A: That is the mean across all four sample requests, not only failures.
explanations.B: That is the larger failed duration, not their mean.
explanations.C: The average is (900 + 1100) divided by two.
explanations.D: That is the sum of failed durations rather than the mean.

stem: The local sample contains four requests, two marked unsuccessful. What failure rate does that sample show?

choices.D: 50 percent

explanations.A: One failure out of four would give 25 percent; the sample has two.
explanations.B: Two of the four requests succeeded.
explanations.C: The failure count is not itself a percentage denominator.
explanations.D: Two failures divided by four requests gives one half.

stem: A read-only Activity log query returns no rows for a short window. What should be checked before concluding that no relevant events exist?

choices.B: Subscription, permissions, time range, filters, and result limits
choices.C: Only whether an Advisor recommendation was dismissed
choices.D: Only the number of workspaces in another tenant

explanations.A: Redundancy does not determine all management-event query scope.
explanations.B: These factors control which records the query can return.
explanations.C: Recommendation state does not validate this log query's scope.
explanations.D: Unrelated tenant workspace counts do not establish the selected Activity log results.

stem: Which event should not be assumed to appear in the Activity log simply because it happened in Azure?

choices.D: A recorded operation's timestamp

explanations.A: Management creation is an appropriate Activity log use.
explanations.B: Blob reads are data-plane events and are not all recorded by the control-plane Activity log.
explanations.C: Operation status is a field exposed by the Activity log query.
explanations.D: Event timestamps are part of Activity log records.

stem: A developer wants to connect a failed request to a slow downstream call. Which telemetry capability is most useful?

choices.D: Correlated application request and dependency traces

explanations.A: Billing currency does not connect execution steps.
explanations.B: Governance compliance does not reveal the request's dependency path.
explanations.C: A lock does not record application transaction relationships.
explanations.D: Correlation supports following a transaction across its observed components.

stem: Application Insights shows no recent request data. Which explanation should be investigated before concluding the application had no users?

choices.A: Instrumentation, collection path, query scope, and time range
choices.B: Application Insights proves all users stopped using every Azure service
choices.C: A workspace automatically records requests from every uninstrumented application
choices.D: A public Azure Status report guarantees each application's request count

explanations.A: Absent displayed telemetry can reflect a data-collection or query-context issue.
explanations.B: A blank application view does not establish a worldwide usage claim.
explanations.C: Collection is not universally automatic for arbitrary applications.
explanations.D: Platform status does not establish an individual application's request telemetry.

stem: Which statement correctly relates KQL and JMESPath in this curriculum?

choices.A: JMESPath creates Log Analytics workspaces whenever --query is used
choices.B: KQL is the PowerShell command used for resource-group deletion
choices.C: KQL analyzes monitoring logs; JMESPath filters Azure CLI JSON output
choices.D: Both languages guarantee that source telemetry has already been collected

explanations.A: A CLI JSON projection does not create a workspace.
explanations.B: KQL is a query language, not that lifecycle command.
explanations.C: The languages serve different query contexts in these exercises.
explanations.D: A query cannot guarantee that its required source data exists.

stem: The lesson presents a KQL datatable containing invented request records. What does reasoning through it demonstrate?

choices.A: That a real Azure collection pipeline has been deployed and tested
choices.B: That an action group notification has been delivered
choices.C: That the production application's latency equals the sample mean
choices.D: Understanding filtering and aggregation on synthetic data

explanations.A: Reading synthetic data does not deploy or validate a collection pipeline.
explanations.B: The example creates no alert or receiver.
explanations.C: Invented records do not establish production measurements.
explanations.D: The exercise teaches query logic without claiming to inspect production telemetry.

stem: Which feature is most appropriate for examining application exceptions and failed requests when telemetry has been collected?

choices.D: Only management-group inheritance

explanations.A: Its application performance experiences support investigating failures and exceptions.
explanations.B: The calculator estimates costs rather than application exceptions.
explanations.C: Resource availability does not provide every custom application's exception context.
explanations.D: Governance hierarchy does not supply request-level failure telemetry.

stem: Why should an alert design name a response owner and investigation procedure?

choices.A: A response owner changes every signal into a cost meter
choices.B: A procedure replaces the need for any collected signal
choices.C: An alert needs an operational response to become useful
choices.D: An owner guarantees that custom code cannot fail

explanations.A: Responsibility assignment does not redefine telemetry as billing.
explanations.B: A monitoring alert still depends on a relevant signal and condition.
explanations.C: A condition and notification alone do not ensure that someone investigates or fixes the issue.
explanations.D: Responsibility does not eliminate application defects.

stem: What should be considered before enabling new log collection or application telemetry in a real environment?

choices.A: Only whether the resource group has a deletion lock
choices.B: Collection requirements, access, retention, and potential cost
choices.C: Only whether the VM has a public IP
choices.D: Assume every amount of ingestion is free indefinitely

explanations.A: Deletion protection alone does not define telemetry collection, privacy, or retention.
explanations.B: A collection design needs appropriate data handling and economic assumptions.
explanations.C: A public IP choice alone does not establish a telemetry collection and retention design.
explanations.D: Monitoring collection and retention can incur charges.

stem: A monitoring design alerts on failure percentage with only one request in its window. What improvement helps avoid misleading percentages?

choices.A: Convert every failed request into a successful record
choices.B: Use only a resource deletion lock
choices.C: Consider a suitable minimum request volume and evaluation window
choices.D: Disable all notifications permanently

explanations.A: Changing evidence would hide real failures.
explanations.B: A lock does not solve the failure-rate denominator issue.
explanations.C: A low denominator can exaggerate a percentage; the design should match actual operating needs.
explanations.D: Removing all alerts does not provide a useful detection design.

stem: Which combination best supports investigating both a recent resource configuration change and a resulting application failure?

choices.A: Activity log management events plus Application Insights telemetry
choices.B: Only a current monthly budget amount
choices.D: Only an empty list of Advisor recommendations

explanations.A: Management history and application observations answer complementary questions.
explanations.B: A budget amount does not record the change or transaction failure.
explanations.C: Geography does not provide management history and request errors.
explanations.D: No optimization findings do not establish either event timeline.
